rationales.A: That is the opposite of what he writes — he says they will never adopt English language or customs.
rationales.B: Franklin calls the Germans 'aliens' and fears them — he is not welcoming them.
rationales.C: Franklin treats German language and customs as something Germans cannot give up — a fixed identity, not a choice.
rationales.D: Franklin never suggests abandoning Pennsylvania — he wants it to stay English.
rationales.general:
1. Read the sentence. The Germans will never adopt our language or customs.
2. Ask what Franklin assumes. That culture is something you are born with, not something you can change.
3. Name the view. Germans are permanently German — and that permanence is what frightens him.
Remember: a claim about what people can never do is a claim about their nature — ask what the writer thinks people are.

stimulus.text: Why should Pennsylvania, founded by the English, become a colony of aliens, who will shortly be so numerous as to Germanize us instead of our Anglifying them, and will never adopt our language or customs, any more than they can acquire our complexion?
